summary.method: Five fresh trials per case/candidate. CPU cost is the median of each trial's server CPU seconds divided by verified private deliveries; query-case CPU includes query work. RSS is the measured phase gate, not peak or kernel memory. Percentiles are histogram upper buckets. All recorded runs, including lower-throughput runs, are retained.

scope: Common application work, native Rust CBOR versus C++ binary protocol; no bridge. Same frozen client, 64 cyclic 1027-byte CBOR byte-string values (1024 application bytes), 16-message windows, 64 private pairs and 8192 idle rooms. C++ treats values as opaque; Rust validates CBOR. Each case runs fresh in a private net namespace, sequentially, pinned to the same server CPU set with client cores separate. Worker/library/build configuration is recorded in cpp_build; active listeners/threads checked for rebuilt C++. Case private: only private traffic. Case churn: private traffic plus fixed-room reconnect workers; every welcome, self delivery, Close/EOF checked, and C++ retired member counts verified before its first 30s GC. Case query: private traffic plus authenticated channel inspectors at fixed intervals, no churn; names/counts and full replies verified, sorting normalized only for C++ which does not promise it. HTTP management has no C++ counterpart. Setup and cleanup gated outside timing, every normal close counted, Rust counters/bytes/reservations checked. Latencies include client validation and concurrent client tasks, logarithmic percentile bucket upper bounds. RSS sampled at gates, not continuous peak/allocated memory. Server/client CPU covers all mixed work. Plaintext loopback, no TLS, rates/heartbeats off, default Rust queues; not a language-only or production-capacity comparison.
limits: Five six-second trials per candidate/workload; all observations including low-throughput repeats retained; no statistical significance claim.
Upstream C++ native optimization flags and Clang 23.1.3 versus the current portable Rust release; original binary protocol versus validated CBOR, with identical application values.
About 8,320 stable users plus query/probe sessions, not a matched 100,000-user C++ capacity or fresh churn test.
RSS sampled at phase gates excludes kernel TCP storage; p99 is the histogram upper bucket including client validation/windowing/scheduling.
Existing idle development services retained; ordinary timing trials have no overlapping builds, profilers or other benchmark loads.
